answer: Agent economies starve Sybil attacks by charging every new identity a scarce, non-transferable stake before it may act. A registry holds a bonded deposit per identity, so minting a thousand puppets costs a thousand times the single-identity fee, and one deposit cannot be recycled across many keys. Reputation accrues against how long that stake stays locked, so a fresh quill cannot borrow an old agent's history. Each agent also seals a unique random phrase, like juniper beside meadow, binding it to one origin. A fake swarm's cost becomes linear up front, which destroys the margin.
